key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings require a trade-off between low friction and high wear resistance through control of barrel filling, gas ratio, and inter-shot delay.
engineering_relevance: Parameter optimization can support wear-resistant surface strengthening and restoration of machine components.
method: Varied barrel filling from 48–68% and working-gas molar ratio O/C from 1.026–1.856.
Evaluated coating morphology, friction, wear, roughness, and hardness.
evidence_signal: Reported results included minimum friction of 0.674 ± 0.136, specific wear rate as low as 0.000189 mm³/(N·m), roughness reduction from 5.00 to 3.60 µm, and maximum hardness of 905.6 HV across tested conditions.
watch_item: The lowest-friction conditions also increased wear, so process settings should be selected for the intended service requirements rather than a single optimum metric.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
